sections:
Think of an ITIN as a tax reference number from the IRS, a little like a UTR from HMRC.

It exists so the IRS can track tax returns and payments for people who are not eligible for a Social Security Number (SSN). It is nine digits long and always begins with 9.

What an ITIN is not matters just as much:

  • It is not permission to work in the US.
  • It does not change your immigration status.
  • It is not an ID card for anything other than tax.

The application form is Form W-7. On it you tick one reason box, such as box b for a nonresident filing a US return.

Most first-time applicants attach a US federal tax return, often Form 1040-NR. Some people qualify for an exception instead, for example when a US payer or bank needs the number for withholding purposes.

You also need proof of identity and foreign status:

  • A valid passport is the only document that works on its own.
  • Otherwise you need two documents from the IRS list of 13.
  • They must be originals or copies certified by the issuing agency. Copies certified by a solicitor or notary are not accepted.

1. Check you need one. Not everyone with a US connection does.
  2. Prepare Form W-7 and your return or exception paperwork.
  3. Have your ID verified. A Certifying Acceptance Agent (CAA) checks your original passport and signs a certificate, Form W-7 (COA). You keep your passport.
  4. The CAA sends the package to the IRS.
  5. Wait for the IRS letter. Your number arrives on notice CP565.

The IRS says to allow about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season (15 January to 30 April) or when applying from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September applications often take about 7 weeks, and from October it is often 4 to 6 weeks. No one can promise a time.

• Sending a solicitor-certified copy of a passport. The IRS will reject it.
  • Applying without a reason. You need a return to file or a valid exception.
  • Posting your original passport to the US when a CAA could check it in the UK.
  • Letting an ITIN lapse. It expires if not used on a US federal return for three tax years in a row.

A CAA is a person or firm authorised by the IRS to help with ITIN applications and to authenticate identity documents.

That last part is the key. Without a CAA, you usually have to post your original passport, or a copy certified by the passport office, to the IRS.

With a CAA, the agent examines your original, completes Form W-7 (COA) to certify it, and sends that certificate with your application. Your passport goes home with you.

A CAA does not issue ITINs. The IRS decides every application.

ITIN Pro UK's IRS Acceptance Agent agreement was approved in October 2026. It started on 6 October 2026 and is valid until 2030. We are not yet shown in the IRS public directory; our listing is pending.

• Your passport. It is the only document accepted on its own.
  • No passport? Two documents from the IRS list, as originals or copies certified by the issuing agency. Solicitor or notary copies will not do.
  • Your reason for applying: a US tax return, or the exception paperwork such as a withholding agent's letter.
  • Children's documents, if you are applying for dependants. For dependants, a CAA can only certify passports and birth certificates.

We cover most of the UK. Around Milton Keynes and Bedford we offer home visits, subject to a travel charge. We can also arrange visits for corporate events, partnerships and company offices.

Where an application suits it, we use a video interview instead. This is also how we help clients in Ireland, Europe, the Middle East and Asia:

  1. You send your original passport (or issuing-agency certified copy) to us by agreed secure, tracked courier.
  2. We hold it during a video interview with you. Additional documents may be requested for video meetings.
  3. We return it by secure tracked post.

A scan or a video call on its own is never enough. The CAA must physically hold the document.

Email us to arrange a flexible meeting. Where significant travel is involved, travel costs are reimbursed by the client.

• Assuming any certified copy will do. Only the issuing agency's certification counts.
  • Booking a passport-only check when you also need the W-7 and return prepared. We provide the full application service, not a stand-alone certificate.
  • Believing anyone who promises approval. No agent can guarantee an ITIN.
  • Leaving it until spring. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks.

sections:
An EIN (Employer Identification Number) identifies a business. An ITIN identifies an individual for tax.

Your LLC needs an EIN to open a US bank account, work with payment platforms and file its own returns. You apply for it on Form SS-4.

A foreign owner with no SSN or ITIN can still get an EIN. The online system often expects a US number, which is why many non-residents apply by fax or post instead.

An ITIN comes into play when you personally have a US filing requirement or someone insists on a personal US tax number. Common triggers:

  • Your LLC is taxed as a partnership (two or more owners). A foreign investor in it needs an ITIN. The LLC generally withholds tax on your share of US business income and reports it on Form 8805; that tax is credited on your Form 1040-NR, which needs an ITIN, so you can reclaim any excess.
  • You must file Form 1040-NR for income effectively connected with a US trade or business.
  • You want to claim a refund of US tax withheld.
  • A US bank, payer or partnership asks for an individual TIN.

If none of these apply, you may not need one at all.

A single-member LLC owned by a non-resident is generally treated as a "disregarded entity". Even so, it has a yearly reporting duty.

  • Form 5472, reporting transactions between the LLC and its foreign owner.
  • A pro-forma Form 1120 as a cover sheet.

This uses the LLC's EIN, not an ITIN. Whether you also need a personal return depends on how and where your income is earned, so take advice on your own facts.

• Applying for an ITIN just to get an EIN. It is usually unnecessary and adds weeks.
  • Ignoring Form 5472. Single-member foreign-owned LLCs must file it even with little activity.
  • Mixing up the numbers on bank or payment forms. The business uses its EIN; you use an ITIN only where a personal TIN is truly required.
  • Assuming no US tax return is needed when you invest in an LLC taxed as a partnership. You need an ITIN and a 1040-NR to reclaim Form 8805 withholding.

sections:
A US partnership reports each partner's share of income on Schedule K-1. To do that properly, it needs a tax number for every partner.

When a partnership earns income connected with a US business, it generally has to withhold tax on a foreign partner's share. It reports that on Form 8805 (or Form 1042-S for some income types).

To get credit for that withholding, the foreign partner files Form 1040-NR, and that return needs an ITIN. If more was withheld than you owe, the excess is refunded.

The same applies to a US LLC taxed as a partnership: a foreign investor in it needs an ITIN to claim the Form 8805 withholding back.

Normally a first-time ITIN application goes with a tax return. Exception 1(a) lets a foreign partner apply earlier, based on the partnership interest itself.

Typical paperwork includes:

  • Form W-7, with Exception 1(a) noted as your reason for applying.
  • A copy of the partnership agreement or similar evidence of your interest, with your name and the partnership's EIN.
  • Your passport, verified by a Certifying Acceptance Agent so you keep the original.

Applying early means your number can be ready before the filing deadline.

1. Gather your K-1, Form 8805 and partnership agreement.
  2. Decide your route: Exception 1(a) now, or W-7 with your first 1040-NR.
  3. Have your passport verified by a CAA.
  4. Send the application and wait: typically 7 to 13 weeks, depending on the season.
  5. Give the ITIN to the partnership and file your 1040-NR to claim credit for tax withheld.

Selling your stake later? A buyer of a partnership interest generally withholds 10% under section 1446(f), so plan ahead.

• Ignoring the K-1 because "it's only a small amount". Withholding you never claim is simply lost.
  • Sending a solicitor-certified passport copy. Only originals or issuing-agency certified copies are accepted.
  • Confusing your ITIN with the partnership's EIN. The partnership has its own number; you need yours.
  • Waiting until a sale to sort out your ITIN, when the 10% withholding is already in play.

sections:
FIRPTA is a US law that makes sure foreign sellers of US property pay their tax.

When a foreign person sells, the buyer generally withholds 15% of the gross sale price, not the profit, and sends it to the IRS on Forms 8288 and 8288-A. Lower rates of 10% or 0% can apply when the buyer will live in the home and the price is up to $1 million or $300,000.

That withholding is a prepayment, not your final bill. If your real tax is lower, you claim the difference back.

• An ITIN for each seller, applied for on Form W-7.
  • Form 1040-NR, reporting the sale and your actual gain.
  • Copy B of Form 8288-A, showing the tax withheld.
  • The sale contract and closing statement.
  • Purchase records and improvement costs, which raise your cost base and reduce your gain.

If you own jointly, each owner normally needs their own ITIN and return. Some US states also withhold on sales, so check your closing statement for state amounts too.

1. Apply for your ITIN. Under Exception 4 you can apply with the sale paperwork rather than a return.
  2. Have your passport verified by a CAA so it stays with you.
  3. Collect Copy B of Form 8288-A once the IRS processes the buyer's filing.
  4. File Form 1040-NR after the tax year ends, with Copy B attached.
  5. Wait for the IRS to process the return and issue any refund.

Haven't closed yet? A Form 8288-B withholding certificate may reduce withholding at closing, and it also needs an ITIN. Form W-7 goes in together with Form 8288-B only when you are applying for a withholding certificate, and certain conditions must be met. See the IRS pages: About Form 8288-B and the Instructions for Form W-7.

• Leaving the ITIN until after the sale. The refund then waits on ITIN processing, which typically takes 7 to 13 weeks depending on the season.
  • Losing Copy B of Form 8288-A. It is your proof of tax paid.
  • Forgetting improvement costs, which can reduce your gain significantly.
  • Only one spouse applying when the property was jointly owned.

sections:
FIRPTA is the US rule that makes a buyer hold back tax when a foreign person sells US property. The starting point is 15% of the gross sale price, not 15% of your profit.

That can be far more than the tax you really owe. Form 8288-B lets you ask the IRS for a withholding certificate, so the amount held back better matches your likely tax bill.

Some lower rates already apply when the buyer will live in the home: 10% or 0% for certain residences up to $1m or $300k. Many US states run their own withholding too, so check yours.

The IRS needs to know exactly who is selling. That means each foreign seller needs a US taxpayer number, which for most UK individuals is an ITIN.

You apply for the ITIN on Form W-7 under Exception 4 (FIRPTA). Form W-7 is filed together with Form 8288-B only when you are applying for a withholding certificate (reduced or no withholding), and certain conditions must be met. See About Form 8288-B and the Instructions for Form W-7 on IRS.gov.

Typical paperwork includes:

  • Form W-7 for each seller named on the deed
  • A copy of the signed sale contract
  • Form 8288-B (or Forms 8288 and 8288-A after closing)
  • Your passport, seen by a Certifying Acceptance Agent, or an original or issuing-agency certified copy

Notarised or solicitor-certified copies are not accepted, which surprises many sellers.

1. Agree the sale and tell your US closing agent you are a foreign seller.
  2. Start the ITIN early. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.
  3. Prepare Form 8288-B with the sale details. Where the conditions are met, your Form W-7 can be filed with it.
  4. At closing, the buyer withholds as required and files Forms 8288 and 8288-A.
  5. After the tax year, you file Form 1040-NR with Copy B of Form 8288-A to claim credit for what was withheld, and a refund of any excess.

With a CAA, your passport is checked in person and handed straight back. It is not posted to the IRS.

• Leaving the ITIN too late. The sale timeline and the IRS timeline rarely line up by luck.
  • Forgetting the second owner. Joint owners each need their own ITIN.
  • Sending notarised copies. They will be rejected.
  • Assuming the 15% is the final tax. It is a prepayment. The real figure is settled on your 1040-NR.

If you are already past closing, read our guide on getting FIRPTA withholding back instead.

sections:
Form 1040-NR is the US federal tax return for nonresident aliens. That covers most people who live in the UK but have some US income or US tax taken from them.

Every return needs a taxpayer number. If you can't get an SSN, that number is an ITIN: a 9-digit number starting with 9, used only for tax.

An ITIN is not a work permit, a visa or a form of US ID.

People we commonly help include those who:

  • had tax withheld and want it back, such as UK residents with US casino winnings
  • sold US property and had FIRPTA tax withheld
  • receive a K-1 from a US partnership with business income
  • had backup withholding after a W-8BEN expired

Not everyone with US income must file. If the right treaty rate was applied at source, there may be nothing to do. Check before you assume.

For a first-time ITIN, the application and the return travel together:

  1. Prepare Form 1040-NR, leaving the ID number space for the IRS to complete.
  2. Complete Form W-7, usually ticking box b (nonresident filing a US return).
  3. Verify identity with your passport. A CAA checks it and returns it to you.
  4. Post the package to the IRS ITIN unit.
  5. Wait for Notice CP565, your ITIN assignment letter. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

A return can't be e-filed in the calendar year your ITIN is issued, so the first one goes on paper.

• Sending the W-7 on its own. Without a return or a valid exception, it will normally be rejected.
  • Using notarised copies of your passport. Only originals or issuing-agency certified copies count.
  • Ignoring Form 1042-S. It shows the US income and tax withheld, and the return relies on it.
  • Filing a 1040 instead of a 1040-NR when you are a nonresident.

The IRS keeps ITINs active only while people use them. If your ITIN is not used on a US federal tax return for three consecutive tax years, it expires on 31 December of the third year.

Renewal usually keeps the same ITIN number.

The good news: you only need to renew when you actually need to file again. If you have no US filing coming up, you can leave it.

Filed with an expired ITIN? The IRS may still process the return under a temporary number, often called a "temporary ITIN". But any refund or credits are held until your ITIN is properly renewed. Renewal usually keeps the same number, so you are not starting from scratch.

Renewal uses the same form as a first application:

  • Form W-7, with the 'Renew an existing ITIN' box ticked and your existing number entered
  • The US tax return you need to file, such as Form 1040-NR
  • Identity documents: your passport, or an original or issuing-agency certified copy of other acceptable documents

Notarised or solicitor-certified copies are not accepted. A Certifying Acceptance Agent can check your passport so it never leaves your hands.

1. Check your last filing year. Look at which tax years you used the ITIN on a return.
  2. Decide if you need to file now. No return due means no renewal yet.
  3. Prepare your return and Form W-7 together.
  4. Verify your ID with a CAA, in person or by agreed courier plus video interview.
  5. Post the package and wait. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

A new assignment letter confirms your ITIN is active again.

• Filing with an expired ITIN and no renewal. The return may be processed under a temporary number, but refunds and credits are held until you renew.
  • Renewing too early, with no return attached and no reason to file.
  • Ticking the wrong box, so the IRS treats it as a new application.
  • Waiting until spring. In our experience, April to July is slowest, at 12 to 13 weeks.

sections:
A US citizen living in the UK still files US tax returns. If they are married to someone who isn't a US citizen or resident, the couple can choose to treat that spouse as a US resident and file jointly under IRC 6013(g).

Every person on a joint return needs a taxpayer number. A spouse who can't get an SSN uses an ITIN.

A spouse may also need an ITIN if they have their own US filing requirement.

Filing jointly means both spouses' worldwide income is taxed in the US. For a British spouse with UK salary, savings or a pension, that is a big change.

For many UK-based couples, foreign tax credits or the foreign earned income exclusion may offset much of the US tax, because UK tax is often higher. But it isn't automatic.

Get the comparison done before you commit. We help with the ITIN; the joint return is quoted separately.

1. Decide on joint filing with your adviser, comparing the options.
  2. Prepare the joint return, with the election made on it.
  3. Complete Form W-7 for the spouse, ticking box e (spouse of a US citizen or resident).
  4. Verify identity. A passport is the only document that works on its own. A CAA checks it and hands it back.
  5. Post the return and Form W-7 together. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

The first joint return can't be e-filed in the year the ITIN is issued, so it goes by post.

• Electing jointly without running the numbers. It can pull UK income into the US system.
  • Sending notarised passport copies. Only originals or issuing-agency certified copies are accepted.
  • Ticking box a or b instead of box e.
  • Applying for an ITIN with no return. The W-7 normally needs the tax return attached.

sections:
A dependant needs an ITIN only if they qualify you for an allowable federal tax benefit and can't get an SSN.

That's the key test. Getting an ITIN just because a form has a box for it doesn't help if no benefit follows.

The ITIN itself gives your child no US status or right to work. It's a tax number and nothing more.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed in July 2025, tightened the Child Tax Credit. It now needs:

  • the child's SSN, valid for work, and
  • the taxpayer's SSN, or at least one spouse's SSN on a joint return.

A child with an ITIN can't bring the Child Tax Credit. They may still give you the $500 Credit for Other Dependents.

Dependants who live outside the US generally don't qualify at all. The main exceptions are residents of Canada or Mexico and certain adopted children. Every family is different, so check with us.

1. Confirm the tax benefit with your adviser first.
  2. Complete Form W-7, ticking box d (dependant of a US citizen or resident) or box g (dependant of a nonresident visa holder).
  3. Gather documents. A passport works on its own, but a US entry date stamp or extra proof of US residency may be needed.
  4. Verify identity. For dependants, a CAA can authenticate only passports and birth certificates.
  5. Post the W-7 with your return. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

• Applying for children who live in the UK with no qualifying benefit. Expect a rejection.
  • Expecting the Child Tax Credit with an ITIN. It now needs an SSN.
  • Missing proof of US residency for a child whose passport lacks a US entry stamp.
  • Sending notarised copies. Only originals or issuing-agency certified copies count.

An ITIN is a 9-digit IRS number for people who need a US tax ID but cannot get a Social Security Number. It is for tax only. It does not give you any immigration status.

US lenders report mortgage interest to the IRS on Form 1098. To do that cleanly, many ask borrowers for a US taxpayer number. If you live in the UK and have no SSN, the ITIN is usually the answer.

Most first-time applicants must attach a US tax return to Form W-7. Exception 3 is different. It covers home mortgage interest reported on Form 1098, so you send evidence of the loan instead.

  • Form W-7, box h, with Exception 3 written in
  • Signed mortgage loan documents or the loan contract
  • Your passport, original or a certified copy from the issuing agency

Solicitor or notary copies are not accepted. With a CAA, your passport is checked and returned to you, not posted to the IRS.

1. Confirm with your lender or broker that the loan will be reported on Form 1098.
  2. Collect the signed loan paperwork once it exists.
  3. Meet a Certifying Acceptance Agent at a home or office visit, or, where it suits your application, courier your original passport for a video interview and get it back by secure tracked post.
  4. The CAA verifies your ID and sends Form W-7 with the certificate of accuracy to the IRS.
  5. Wait for your CP565 letter. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

If you later rent the property out, the same ITIN is used on your Form 1040-NR.

• Sending loan papers that are unsigned. The IRS wants evidence of a real mortgage loan.
  • Using a solicitor-certified passport copy. Only originals or issuing-agency copies count.
  • Applying for both borrowers on one form. Each borrower needs their own Form W-7.
  • Forgetting the rental angle. Rental income or a future sale may bring US filing duties, so keep your ITIN active.

When a nonresident is paid for personal services, like lecturing, consulting or performing, US payers generally withhold tax. A tax treaty may exempt that pay.

Form 8233 is how you claim that treaty exemption with the US payer. It asks for a US taxpayer number. If you cannot get a Social Security Number, you need an ITIN.

Normally a first-time Form W-7 must include a US tax return. Exception 2(a) lets you apply without one when you claim a treaty benefit on wages or honoraria.

  • Form W-7, ticking box h and writing "Exception 2(a)". Where you claim a treaty benefit, also tick box a and enter the treaty country and article
  • Your completed Form 8233
  • A signed letter from the US payer about the work and payment
  • Your passport, original or an issuing-agency certified copy

Notarised or solicitor-certified copies are not accepted.

1. Ask the US payer exactly what they need and by when.
  2. Complete Form 8233 and request the payer's letter.
  3. Book a Certifying Acceptance Agent: a home or office visit, or, where it suits, a video interview with your passport couriered to us and returned by secure tracked post.
  4. The CAA verifies your ID and sends Form W-7 with the certificate of accuracy to the IRS.
  5. Your CP565 letter arrives. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

• Leaving it too late. Processing takes weeks, so start once the engagement is confirmed.
  • Using Form W-8BEN for service fees. Form 8233 is the form for treaty relief on personal services pay.
  • A vague payer letter. It should be signed and clearly about your engagement.
  • Assuming every fee is exempt. Treaty rules have conditions, so check with us before you rely on them.

Students on F-1 or J-1 visas often cannot work, so they cannot get a Social Security Number. But scholarship and fellowship money can still have US tax consequences.

Universities may need a US tax ID to report the payment or apply a treaty benefit. That number is the ITIN. It is for tax only and does not give you permission to work.

First-time applicants usually attach a tax return to Form W-7. Exceptions 2(b) and 2(c) cover certain scholarships and fellowships, so you can apply without one. Exception 2(b) applies when you claim a treaty benefit.

  • Form W-7, ticking box f for students, professors and researchers
  • A signed letter from your school or its designated school official (DSO)
  • Your passport, original or an issuing-agency certified copy

Notarised or solicitor copies are refused.

1. Ask your international office which exception applies and what their letter will say.
  2. Get the signed letter from the school or DSO.
  3. Meet a Certifying Acceptance Agent at a home or office visit, or, where it suits your application, courier your original passport for a video interview and get it back by secure tracked post.
  4. The CAA checks your ID and sends Form W-7 with the certificate of accuracy to the IRS.
  5. Wait for your CP565 letter. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

• Posting your passport before term. With a CAA, you keep it, which matters when you need to travel.
  • A missing or unsigned school letter. The exception depends on it.
  • Applying in spring. Mid-January to April is the busiest season.
  • Assuming the ITIN is permanent. It expires if unused on a federal return for three consecutive tax years.

US payers generally withhold 30% on royalties paid to nonresidents. Under the US–UK tax treaty, royalties paid to UK residents are usually taxed at 0% in the US.

To get that treaty rate, you give the payer Form W-8BEN. It confirms you are not a US person and claims the treaty benefit.

Many UK residents can claim the treaty rate on Form W-8BEN using a foreign tax number, such as a UTR or National Insurance number, on line 6a. Line 5 is for a US number. So you may not need an ITIN just for the form.

You usually do need one when:

  • You must file a Form 1040-NR to reclaim tax already withheld
  • Your payer insists on a US tax ID. A signed letter from them on letterhead may support an Exception 1(d) application without a return

1. Check your Form 1042-S to see the income and tax withheld.
  2. Update your Form W-8BEN so future payments get the treaty rate.
